decisions.issues: Minor only: the yard figures mostly face the house rather than clearly looking up at the wall, and the fort flies a plain white flag instead of the Travancore conch-on-red standard (the same white flag appears in panels 2, 4 and 5, so the page is consistent). Ridges, red earth, gold grass, village smoke, laterite wall behind bamboo scaffolding with masons, and the tiled house among pepper vines all match. No text, gore or anachronism. Large clear sky at upper left for both captions.

Minor only. A thin maroon cord, read as a sword belt, shows at the waist under the mundu folds. It is not a broad red sash. The trader's towel is on his right shoulder here and on his left in panel 1.3. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch23 row: Kerala topknot with grey at the temples, no turban, thick curled moustache, clean chin, tiny gold stud, silver chain, talwar at his left hip, cream shoulder cloth. The trader matches the script: grey beard, bare head and chest, checked lungi, towel, clay cup, talking up at Nagoji. The flag is plain white and the art has no text. Open sky at upper centre and upper right leaves room for all three balloons.

The trader does not quite match panel 1.2. Here he has short curly grey hair, a close-trimmed beard and a heavier build. In 1.2 his hair is longer and swept back, and his beard is fuller. His towel has also moved to the other shoulder. He is not a principal, he still fits the script description, and the reader can take him as the same man, so this is acceptable. The beat works: he is close, shrugs with an open palm and holds a clay cup of buttermilk. The courtyard, laterite wall and tiled verandah match 1.2. The oil lamp is clay with an open flame. Both hands are sound and there is no text. Clear sky in the upper right gives room for the long and medium balloons, away from his face and the shrugging hand.

Acceptable, with minor deviations: Ramayyan writes with a stylus on the palm-leaf bundle instead of tapping his fingers on it. Varma's hair knot sits low at the back of his head behind the near (right) ear rather than as a side knot above the left ear, though he is clearly bare-headed with no turban or crest. Varma looks off-panel to the right instead of straight at the reader, which still works spatially because the courtyard where Nagoji stood in panel 1.2 lies to the right of the verandah. Both faces match their sheets. Hands are sound. No text. The hanging brass lamp has an open wick. Clear sky at upper right, and a plain wall with roof beams at upper left, give room for both Ramayyan balloons.

Clean. The face matches the V13 Varma sheet: thick moustache, pearl drop earrings and gold bead necklaces. He is bare-headed with his hair in a knot above and behind his LEFT ear, with no turban, crest or crown. He is bare-chested under a cream cloth with a gold border. The border pattern is geometric, not pseudo-text. There is no bandage, which is correct because the knife wound comes later in the chapter. He shows a faint amused smirk, set in the same laterite courtyard and verandah. Open sky in the upper left takes both balloons clear of his face.

Clean on the main checks. Nagoji has a topknot, grey at the temples, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a small round gold stud on the lobe with nothing hanging from it, a silver chain, a cream mundu and shoulder cloth, and no turban or sash. He rides Kayal, a bay with black points and no white markings. Padmini rides beside him in a cream sari with a gold border and no blouse, with simple gold, the thick hair coiled at the nape and the staff laid across her saddle. The column is all there: turbaned riders with tall spears on dark horses, musketeers in white on foot with long matchlocks, and a brass light gun on a carriage with bullocks, on a red dirt track. There is no text, blood or European kit, and the large clear sky upper right holds both the caption and the balloon. Minor points: Padmini's hair is more grey than 'black threaded with grey'. Her staff is a turned pole with brass bands, where her sheet shows a knobbly natural stick, so at a glance it reads a little like a musket barrel. She and Nagoji wear riding boots. The Nair musketeers wear turbans, where bare-headed topknots would be more accurate. The forearm scar is not visible. None of these is disqualifying.

Minor: Padmini's hair reads almost all black in the dusk light, with little of the grey threading that the ch16-27 row and the neighbouring panels 2.1 and 2.5 show. Everything else matches the beat: a Kerala gatehouse with a low tiled roof and carved gable figures, cloths between trees, wall-niche oil lamps, drummers and pipers, girls carrying the flower-decked goddess palanquin, older women with brass plates, Padmini dismounted in the line with a clay lamp and her stick, and men bowing. No painted text. Clear dusk sky at top centre for the caption.

Minor: the brand patch and long white scar are correctly on Nagoji's LEFT forearm, but they sit on the outer side near the elbow rather than on the inner forearm a hand's width above the wrist, and there is an extra long pale scar on his left upper arm. Ponnan has a tiny ear stud, and his horse is the same size as Kayal rather than a head lower. These are small. Nagoji matches his sheet (topknot, grey temples, gold ear stud, clean chin, thick curled moustache, silver chain), and so does Ponnan (curly hair, no topknot, moustache, clean chin, red shoulder cloth, short jacket, spear). The tusker with its gold nettipattam and children offering bananas is present. Dusk sky across the top centre takes both balloons above the heads.

Minor: the sweet fried discs are drawn as glazed rings that look a little like pretzels, though they pass as fried festival sweets. Yusuf matches the bible (tall, lean, white skullcap, trimmed dark beard, short dark coat over a white tunic, no turban, no scar). He keeps one hand on the basket, steadies the startled boy with the other and smiles up toward someone out of frame. Same festival setting, lamps and elephant as 2.2 and 2.3. Open sky at upper left and centre takes both captions.

Page continuity: Padmini's horse has a broad white blaze and a lighter reddish coat, while in 2.1 v01 she rides a plain dark bay. The 2.1 correction asks for the blaze, so the two will match after regeneration. Otherwise this matches the beat: Padmini back at her horse with lamp-lit wall and the procession behind her, eyes bright, grey-threaded hair, gold, cream sari with gold border and her stick. No painted text, and the hands on the bridle and stick are sound. The dusk sky and trees at top centre can take her balloon clear of her face.

Minor only. Nagoji matches: topknot with grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold ear stud, silver chain, cream shoulder cloth, no turban or red sash. He wears a sheathed sword at the hip, which is not a knife. Kayal is a bay with black points and no white markings. Ponnan matches (curly hair, moustache, clean chin, red shoulder cloth, spear) but wears an ochre jacket, while in 3.4 he wears a red, gold-trimmed tunic as on his sheet. The covered dead wear heavy leather boots and belts that read a little soldierly, but no faces or blood show. The large clear sky at upper right takes both Ponnan balloons.

Minor only. Nagoji stands dismounted, while 3.1 shows him mounted; the script does not specify either way. A faint shadow of stubble on the chin still reads as clean-shaven. The checked cloth and coins lie on the ground instead of in Ponnan's hand. A round brand and scar show on the left forearm, which the ch23 bible row allows. Otherwise the panel matches: topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, flush gold ear stud, silver chain, raided convoy setting, and a gaze toward the hills. The sky top centre and right is clear for both balloons.

Clean. Spearmen and archers stand across the road, with matchlockmen on both slopes holding smoking slow-match at their wrists. The plain green banners carry no writing, and the raja sits on a low stool in the centre of the road. He is drawn a little larger than 'very small' but still reads as distant. Some raiders wear white head cloths. The pale sky between the slopes is clear for both captions.

Minor only. The shot is over the shoulder from behind Nagoji: topknot, grey temples, gold stud, cream gold-bordered shoulder cloth, inclined head, with Kayal's bay ears and black mane below. Ponnan's spear and red cloth are at the left edge. The grey-haired, grey-moustached, bare-chested Nair captain with a round shield is at the right edge. The raja sits centred, facing us, heavy, with gold ear hoops, chains, a gold-edged sash and a sword at the sash, and he does not rise. Ponnan's visible sleeve is a red, gold-trimmed tunic (his sheet look), unlike the ochre jacket in 3.1. Nagoji's tail point is his hidden mouth beside the ear, since he faces away. The sky between the banners is clear for three balloons.

Minor only. The raja spreads his hands, at ease on his stool, with grinning spearmen behind and matchlockmen and plain green banners on the slopes. He shows gold ear hoops, chains, a gold-edged sash and a sword at the sash. His chin carries a light dark stubble that is not in 3.4. His second foot is hidden under the long mundu. The ground is redder than the pale road in 3.3 and 3.4. Nagoji speaks from off panel, and the raja glances to the viewer's left, so that line's tail points to the left frame edge. The large open sky takes all three balloons.

Clean pick. It is a true close-up, as the r1 correction asked. Brows are lowered, the lids narrowed a fraction and the eyes cut sideways. He has long black hair swept back loose with no bun, a thick moustache, a clean chin, heavy gold ear hoops, several neck chains and a bare chest. Behind him are a red-earth slope, a plain green banner and spearmen in indigo head cloths. The upper-left third is open blue sky for both balloons, and there is no text. Minor: his eyes cut toward frame right, not frame left, so the off-panel Nagoji tail points to the upper right edge. One barely visible figure at the far right edge has a reddish head cloth.

Acceptable, and it fixes the r1 failures. There is no stool in the road and no yellow flags. The slope men are bare-chested in indigo head cloths under plain green banners, and the foreground musketman's matchlock glows correctly at the lock, not at the muzzle. Nagoji has the topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, cream shoulder cloth with gold border over his left shoulder and the silver chain. His open palm is raised and his eyes are not on Ponnan. Ponnan has curly hair, a moustache, the red shoulder cloth, a short jacket and a spear, on a smaller horse. Kayal is bay with a black mane. Minor points: Nagoji's ear stud is a tiny gold bead at the lobe, which still reads as a stud. Faint pale streaks on his raised RIGHT inner forearm could read as a scar on the wrong arm, but they are only a few pixels. The distant column behind the riders wears dark head cloths with crossed belts and carries spears, a little unlike the white-turbaned Nairs of 4.3. A few distant slope men wear dark vests. There is sky at top centre and right for the two balloons.

The composition works: reverse wide over the raja's bare back and gold-edged sash, Nagoji on Kayal, Nair musketeers with crossed belts, the small gun on its bullock carriage, matchlocks and green banners on both slopes, and open sky for the balloons. Nagoji's face is correct (clean chin, curled moustache, gold ear stud, topknot). Several things rule it out. (1) Nagoji is bare-chested with no cream shoulder cloth. That is a costume break from 3.1, 3.4 and 4.2 and contradicts the chapter 23 bible row (mundu with shoulder cloth). (2) From behind, the raja's hair is a curly mass with a gold-ringed topknot bun, unlike the long swept-back hair in 3.4, 3.5, 4.1, 4.4 and 4.5. (3) Nagoji points sideways at the slope rather than back the way they came. (4) A yellow flag flies in the Travancore column. (5) The mark on Nagoji's inner left forearm is dark and tattoo-like instead of a pale healed patch.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition. Keep the raja's broad bare back, gold-edged sash, gold ear hoop and wooden stool in the left foreground. Keep Nagoji on Kayal at right centre, and behind him the white-clad Nair musketeers with crossed leather belts and the small gun on its bullock carriage. Keep the matchlock men and plain green banners on both slopes and the open sky at top centre. Fix four things. First, from behind, the raja's hair must match the other panels: long, sleek black hair swept straight back from the brow and falling loose to the shoulders, with no topknot, no bun, no hair ring and no beard showing at the jaw. Second, Nagoji wears his cream shoulder cloth draped over his left shoulder and across his chest, over the white mundu, with the silver chain on top, as in panels 3.4 and 4.2. He is not bare-chested. Keep his topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin and small gold ear stud. Third, Nagoji half-turns in the saddle and gestures back over his shoulder, open hand, toward the road behind him and the column, not sideways at the slope. Any mark on his inner left forearm is only a faint, pale, healed patch, never a dark tattoo. Fourth, the Travancore column carries no yellow or saffron flag: show either no banner or a plain red standard with a silver conch and no writing.

decisions.issues: The raja's downcast eyes, ear hoops and neck chains are right. Three problems rule it out. (1) The convoy wreckage is placed in the valley right beside the raja's stool: an overturned cart, dead harnessed bullocks, barrels, a brass pot and a maroon cloth. This contradicts 3.1 and 4.3, where the convoy died on another stretch of road and Nagoji gestures back to it, and it breaks the clean road of 4.1 and 4.5. (2) The rendering drifts to a semi-photographic painted look, unlike the inked style of the rest of the page. (3) The shot is framed waist-up, not close.
decisions.correction: Remove all convoy wreckage from the valley: no cart, no fallen or dead bullocks, no barrels, sacks, pots, scattered goods or red or maroon cloth anywhere. The convoy died on a different stretch of road (panel 3.1), so the road around the raja shows the same clean red-earth road, line of bare-chested spearmen in indigo head cloths, matchlock slopes and plain faded green banners as panels 4.1 and 4.5. Frame him truly close: head and shoulders to mid-chest, face large in the right half of the frame. Keep the expression from the last attempt: eyes dropped and cut down toward frame left, as if toward the far road out of frame, mouth and jaw still slack, not yet set. Keep his long black hair swept back loose to the shoulders, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin, heavy gold ear hoops and gold neck chains. Draw it in the book's inked graphic-novel style, with clean ink line and painted colour matching panels 4.1 and 4.5, not a semi-photographic rendering. Leave the upper-left part of the frame as open sky or soft slope with no faces, for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Clean pick. The raja leans forward on the stool with a clenched scowl. His look is right: bare chest, gold ear hoops and chains, gold-edged sash, worn-hilted sword. The slopes are consistent with page 3 (matchlocks, green banners, indigo head cloths). The sepia inset with its hard border reads clearly as Colachel: palms, powder smoke, spearmen and Nairs in one line. There is no text. Minor points: one musketman at top right wears a maroon head cloth, though red is reserved for Ponnan, and the stool is plainer than the carved one in 4.1. The three balloons fit in the open sky at upper centre (x 0.25 to 0.70, y 0 to 0.2) and the low-detail hills below it. The caption sits in the inset's sky.

Minor only. The raja is visible small and far off on his stool, though the prompt said he is outside the frame. That fits the valley geography, so I let it stand. The slow-match is drawn smouldering at the musket muzzles, not at the wrists. A few spearmen wear thin shoulder straps. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch23 row: topknot, grey temples, flush gold stud, thick moustache, clean chin, cream gold-bordered shoulder cloth and silver chain. Kayal's ochre-bay head with black mane is in the foreground. The open sky at top centre takes both Nagoji balloons.

Usable, with minor issues. Nagoji is seen past his shoulder, mounted on the ochre-bay Kayal, but he and the horse face into the scene toward his own column, so the raja's point of view is loose. The present-day Padmini shows black hair with no visible grey (the prompt asked for black). The quiet band above the inset is tight. The letterer should use the pale sky strip at the top of the inset (about x 0.63-0.86, y 0.61-0.70) and the empty road between Kayal's head and the inset (about x 0.51-0.62, y 0.63-0.95) for the two remembered lines, keeping both young faces clear. The inset itself works: young Padmini with black hair points her stick at a leaner young Kollamkara with gold ear hoops, chains, a gold-edged sash and a sword. The Travancore musketeers and the bullock-drawn gun match page 4.

Minor only. The slow-match on the slope muskets burns at the muzzle tips instead of at the wrists. The raja matches his bible line: heavy and bare-chested, gold hoops and chains, gold-edged sash, sword at the sash, long loose curls like 5.1 and 5.4. His shoulders are tight and he glances sideways, which is the script beat. Nagoji is off panel, so his two tails point to the left edge, matching his position on the left in 5.4. There is a large empty sky for all three balloons.

v01 (only candidate): the composition, Kayal (correct ochre bay with black points, no white markings) and the raja (bare-chested, gold-edged sash, ear hoops, chains, sword, long wavy hair, looking up) are all good, and there is clear sky upper centre for both lines. But Nagoji is bare-chested with no cream shoulder cloth. The chapter's bible row ('cream or white mundu with shoulder cloth') and the chapter lock require it, and he wears it in 5.1, 5.2 and 5.5, so he changes costume between consecutive panels on the same page. Face, topknot, grey temples, ear stud, moustache, clean chin and silver chain are correct.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition exactly: Kayal (ochre red-brown bay with black mane, tail and lower legs, quilted ochre saddle pad) standing on the left with Nagoji mounted, and the Kollamkara Raja seated on his carved stool on the right looking up at him. Keep the indigo-clad spearmen, the plain green banners, the musketmen on the slopes and the open sky in the upper centre. Fix only Nagoji's costume to match the neighbouring panels. A cream shoulder cloth with a narrow gold border is draped over his left shoulder and across his chest, over the white mundu, with the silver chain of office visible over it. He is not bare-chested. Keep his face, Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, small gold ear stud, thick curled moustache and clean-shaven chin as they are.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Soft smoke drifts from the muzzles of the aiming musketmen on both slopes; it can read as a recent shot, though there is no muzzle flash. The raja sits behind Nagoji rather than facing him, a common foreground-speaker staging. Nagoji's head sits in the upper half of the strip with the topknot touching the top edge, so do not crop from the top. Nagoji is close and level: topknot, grey temples, flush gold stud, thick curled moustache, smooth clean chin, cream gold-bordered shoulder cloth and silver chain. Open sky at upper centre-right takes the balloon.

v01 is otherwise strong. It shows the right valley road, plain green banners and the raja heaving himself up off his stool, and Nagoji is right on Kayal: topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, silver chain, cream shoulder cloth and a tiny gold stud on the lobe. The sky also leaves a large clear space for both balloons. It fails the bible on the brand. His LEFT forearm, the one on the reins nearest the viewer, shows its outer face, and that face carries a long white slash with a short crossbar near the elbow. At print size it reads as a cross or dagger mark. The bible puts the brand and scar on the INNER left forearm a hand's width above the wrist, as a puckered patch that is explicitly not a cross. The script for this panel does not need the brand at all.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition: the raja rising from his low stool at the centre of the road, Nagoji on Kayal at left, the spearmen, the matchlock men on both slopes, the plain green banners and the open sky above. Fix one detail. Nagoji's LEFT forearm, on the reins nearest the viewer, shows its outer face, and that outer face must be plain, unmarked skin from elbow to wrist. Draw no white line, slash, crossbar or cross-, sword- or letter-shaped mark anywhere on either arm. The old brand and the long white scar sit only on the inner face of the LEFT forearm, a hand's width above the wrist. That face is turned toward the horse's neck and is not visible in this panel. Keep the tiny flush gold stud clearly on his visible earlobe, with nothing hanging from it.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. The wide shot works: the raja waves a raised hand while his spearmen stand in two lines with the road open down the middle. The banners are plain green, there is no text and no blood, the hands are sound, and the open sky gives plenty of room for both of his balloons. One minor continuity drift: here the raja has a short dark chin beard and a small red dot on his forehead. In 5.2 to 5.4 and in 6.1 he has a moustache and stubble only. The bible sets no beard rule for him. A few spearmen also wear olive-green cloth and head cloths, where the bible asks for indigo or earth-brown.

The two riders work. Ponnan has curly hair, a moustache, the red shoulder cloth, a short jacket and a spear, and he turns toward Nagoji. Nagoji, on Kayal, has the topknot, grey temples, clean chin and silver chain. But the rest of the valley contradicts 6.1 and 6.2 and the raja's bible line. (1) A bearded, turbaned chief in a white jama and gold sash sits on a dais in the centre of the road, where the raja's stool stood. He reads as the Kollamkara Raja, but the raja is bare-chested and bare-headed and has no beard elsewhere. (2) The lining troops wear white tunics with yellow sashes, crossed belts and white turbans under bright yellow banners. In 6.1 and 6.2 they are bare-chested men in indigo with plain green banners, and the crossed belts make them read as Travancore regulars. (3) Nagoji's RIGHT wrist has a pinkish scar band. (4) Ponnan's horse is as big as Kayal, though it should be a head lower. (5) The spear points do not crowd close to the riders as the script asks.
decisions.correction: Keep the two riders as drawn: Ponnan at left with curly hair, the red shoulder cloth and a spear, leaning toward Nagoji, who rides Kayal at right with his topknot and silver chain. Change the valley to match the two previous panels. The raja's men lining both sides of the road are bare-chested spearmen in dark indigo and earth-brown cloth, with indigo or brown head cloths and round dark shields. They wear no white tunics, no yellow sashes and no crossed belts, and their spear points crowd in close on both sides of the riders. All banners are plain faded green, never yellow. Do not draw any seated, turbaned or bearded chief, dais or throne in the road. If the raja appears at all, he is small in the far distance, standing beside his low wooden stool: heavy, bare-chested and bare-headed, with loose curly hair, a moustache and no beard, in a white mundu with a gold-edged sash. Nagoji's right wrist and forearm are plain skin with no band, scar or mark. Ponnan rides a smaller Maravar horse whose head sits about a head lower than Kayal's.

decisions.issues: Clean and on script. The wide high-ridge view shows thick black smoke columns over torched pepper gardens and support poles along a canal. Raiders in plain earth-brown and cream cloth with indigo head cloths walk away unhurried down a scrub path at right. There are no bodies, no red cloth, no muskets or blue coats, and no painted text. The smoke-dimmed grey sky across the top band, especially the paler haze at upper left and centre, holds all three captions. Two minor points: the raiders wear plain shirts rather than going bare-chested, and the two nearest are somewhat close to the ridge rather than far below, but both still read as small, distant figures.

Acceptable. Padmini matches her sheet and the chapter 16 to 27 row: cream sari with a gold border in the old Kerala drape with no blouse, gold ear studs and necklace, grey threading through her black hair, and her long walking stick gripped hard in her right hand while her left hand is clenched. The burned gardens read clearly: torched vines, cut poles and trampled red soil, with the canal at left. Two men lie still, with no wounds, and a farmer draws a cloth over one. The raiders are small on the far ridge. The dark smoke sky above and right of her head leaves room for her two balloons and the caption. Minor: the farmer wears a stitched olive short-sleeved shirt with rolled sleeves where a shoulder cloth would be more typical, and Padmini's hair sits loose and curly rather than in a clear coil at the nape.

Minor issues, acceptable. The gun locks are generic and show no slow-match, but none is clearly a flintlock or percussion lock. The grey-horse rider is falling back, hands at his chest, rather than fully thrown clear. On the cream horse, the rider's foot caught in the stirrup is readable but not emphatic. There is no blood, no text, and no lettering is needed.

Minor: Nagoji wears tall black riding boots here, while in panel 7.5 they are dark brown ankle boots. Nagoji is otherwise on model: topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, flush ear stud, silver chain. Kayal has no white markings.

Acceptable, with minor issues. Ponnan matches his sheet (curly hair, moustache, clean chin, red gold-trimmed jacket and red shoulder cloth, white mundu at bare knees). His horse is a bay with a white star, distinct from Kayal. The cut stirrup strap is implied rather than shown. The tiny far body in the road has an odd leg arrangement and a red waist cloth, so it reads more like a fallen rider than the bare-chested shooter. Three ambushers at top left are still firing. The flank riders at right show their backs as well as the spear points. There is no blood, no text, and no lettering is needed.

Minor: Nagoji's ear ornament is a tiny gold bead that sits just below the lobe. It reads as a stud at page size. Background Travancore riders and one dead ambusher wear small, dull maroon waist cloths, which slightly dilute 'red cloth is Ponnan's alone'. They are small and do not compete with Ponnan's red. The face-down dead ambushers at lower right show no blood.

Clean. Nagoji matches sheet and ch23 row: topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, silver chain of office, cream shoulder cloth, white mundu, no turban or sash, and a pale scar line on the inner left forearm. Kayal is correct (bay, black mane, black lower legs, ochre quilted pad). Ponnan has curly hair, moustache, red shoulder cloth, short jacket, spear, bare knees, on a smaller horse. Late-afternoon ridge over thorn and rock valley, gun cart and riders behind. Minor only: one tiny background man on the right wears a red head cloth, and Ponnan seems to have a small ear stud that is not on his sheet. Open sky top right and above Ponnan takes the balloon.

Clean. Padmini matches her sheet and the ch16-27 row: black hair threaded with grey and coiled at the nape, gold ball earring and bead necklace, cream sari with a gold border, no blouse, and a long walking stick in her right hand. She rides at the rear of the column with a hard, flinty look. The bullock-drawn gun and the riders lead away along the ridge, and the late-afternoon sky gives wide clear space at the top and upper right for all three balloons. Nagoji is off panel, so his tail goes to the right edge toward the head of the column.

Acceptable. Nagoji's Kerala topknot has grey at the temples, with no turban and no sash. He wears a white mundu with a gold-bordered shoulder cloth and a silver chain. His moustache is thick and curled, his chin clean-shaven, and a small gold bead sits at the ear lobe. Sweating crew haul on the rope, and the gun captain sights along the barrel at the scrub valley. One minor flaw: the gun captain's face nearly touches the cascabel, which reads a little awkward but still says 'sighting'. The sky at the upper right and centre is open for Nagoji's balloon. The sunset light matches 8.2.

Acceptable. This wide shot carries the full beat: the gunner touches the linstock to the vent, flame bursts from the muzzle, a great bank of smoke rolls out, and a flock of birds bursts up over the trees across the thorn valley. The crew are sound, there is no text and no gore, and the large open sky across the top suits the long caption. Two minor flaws. The sky is bluer and brighter than the sunset glow of 8.2 and 8.3, though warm light still shows on the right horizon. The bullock yoke is still hitched just behind the gun carriage.

Acceptable. Nagoji matches sheet and ch23 row: topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, silver chain, cream shoulder cloth, white mundu, no turban or sash. He is on foot with his talwar drawn, leading spearmen down off the ridge into the thorn, with the gun and riders left on the crest. Hands and sword grip are sound. Minor: a small rider top left wears a rust-red turban, and the small spearman at lower right wears a red head cloth. Both are against the chapter's red-for-Ponnan rule, but they are distant, and Nagoji is unmistakably the foreground figure. Open sky top right takes both the 'Now.' balloon and the caption.

Minor only: the light is a little brighter than the script's 'dim', and the ball is drawn still in flight next to leaves it has already shredded. Nagoji is on model: topknot, grey temples, clean-shaven chin, flush gold stud, white mundu with shoulder cloth, silver chain, no turban or sash. The raider in the background with an indigo head cloth and matchlock is acceptable. No text, no blood, and the hands are sound.

Minor: the elbow is already touching the spearman's jaw, slightly past 'the instant before contact'. Otherwise the beat reads well: the spear point scrapes past his hip as he twists into the elbow strike. Nagoji is on model (topknot, grey temples, clean chin, gold stud, silver chain, mundu), and the faint pale scar shows on the inner left forearm. Both men's hands have five fingers and are correct. No text or blood.

Clean. Two dark silhouettes stand against a wall of white powder smoke. Rim light picks out the ash smeared on the raider's face as he holds his sword high, and Nagoji steps inside the swing. Nagoji keeps his topknot, grey temples, moustache, clean chin and gold stud. In the background a third raider with a dagger slips as loose stones scatter. Torn cloth strips flutter from the raider's arm, which reads as plausible. No text, no blood, and the setting matches the neighbouring panels.

Acceptable. Nagoji matches the lock: hair gathered into a topknot on the crown, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin (soot specks only), small gold ear stud, silver chain, cream shoulder cloth over the LEFT shoulder (consistent with 9.1). He is drawn chest-up and close with soot and sweat. The three raiders lie still behind him with no wounds: the spearman left, the swordsman centre, the dagger man right. Minor points: (1) the topknot is looser than in 9.1, with more hair hanging at the sides; (2) the dead raiders are rendered sharp rather than in soft focus; (3) the left spearman's spear butt disappears behind his head (it reads as planted in the ground, not as a wound, but the letterer could check it at print size); (4) the shoulder cloth here is plain white, without the gold border seen in 9.1. For the two captions, the top-right corner over the cliff and smoke (about x 0.66 to 0.98, y 0.02 to 0.20) is clear and covers no face or key action. The top-left thorn corner is a second option.

Clean. The boy is thin and beardless with a small hair knot and a torn brown shoulder cloth. He is backed against a pale rock face, holds no sword, raises both hands (five fingers each) and shows terror in his wide eyes. A large, low-detail stretch of rock wall at the upper right gives room for the BOY balloon. No text, no blood, and no other figures.

Minor: the talwar is in his right hand here but in his left in 10.4. The fallen raiders lie on muted red-brown cloth that does not read as blood. The silver chain has a different link and pendant design from 10.2 and 10.4. Identity is clean: topknot, grey temples, tiny flush gold stud, curled moustache, clean chin, soot streaks. Open sky at upper right takes the caption and Nagoji's balloon.

Minor: the forearm scar on his raised LEFT arm is pinkish instead of white and sits near the elbow. The boy's hair reads as a messy crown bun plus a small knot at the nape. Matches the beat: a low angle from behind the boy, talwar high against a white sky, the boy shrinking with his hands up. The large white sky at upper right takes the caption.

None significant. A tight insert: Ponnan's arm, in a red short sleeve with a gold border and with the edge of the red shoulder cloth, enters from the right and clamps Nagoji's wrist just above the hilt. Nagoji's forearm shows the long pale scar running along it. Ponnan entering from the right matches his screen position in 10.4. Open sky at upper left takes the off-panel balloon, with its tail toward the top-right corner.

Minor: the brand on Nagoji's inner LEFT forearm is a small dark ink blot, not a pale puckered patch. It is on the correct arm, with the pale scar running along the forearm. Three hands are stacked on the wrist and hilt, and they resolve correctly. Ponnan matches his sheet: curly hair with no topknot, red jacket and shoulder cloth, hitched mundu, bare knees, soot on the face. Nagoji has a cocked right fist, ready to strike. The sky at upper right and the foliage band at upper left take the two short balloons.

Ponnan is on-model (curly hair, moustache, clean chin, red jacket and shoulder cloth) and grips Nagoji's wrist with his mouth open. But this is a medium two-shot, not the close shot on Ponnan the script calls for. Nagoji sits on the ground instead of standing as in 10.4. The gripped hand is an empty fist, so the talwar has vanished between panels. Nagoji has no silver chain of office, which the chapter 23 bible row requires. Two living armed men walk through the background with matchlocks, which pulls focus from the confrontation.
decisions.correction: Make this a CLOSE shot on Ponnan, chest-up, filling the left two-thirds of the frame. He stands upright, face streaked with soot, eyes clear and hard, mouth open mid-word. Keep his look: curly hair, no topknot, thick moustache, clean chin, short deep-red jacket with gold-edged short sleeves, red shoulder cloth. His fist still clamps Nagoji's wrist in the lower foreground, and Nagoji's hand still grips the single talwar hilt with the blade pointing DOWN. Nagoji stands at the right edge, partly cropped, NOT seated: topknot, grey at the temples, small gold ear stud, curled moustache, clean chin, the silver chain of office on his bare soot-streaked chest, cream shoulder cloth over a white mundu. Background: thorn and pale powder smoke only, with no other living figures. Keep the upper area of smoke and sky clear for two speech balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor only: the chain of office is a heavy coin-and-medallion chain here but a thin beaded chain in 11.4. The brand on the inner left forearm is a small dark circular mark rather than a pale puckered patch, though it has no letters and no cross. The dead raiders lying nearby are a heavier aftermath than the script asks for, but there is no blood. Nagoji matches his sheet and the chapter 23 row (topknot, grey at the temples, gold stud, curled moustache, clean chin, white mundu and shoulder cloth, dark dulled talwar). The boy sobs against the rock. The pale sky at the top centre and top right takes the caption and Nagoji's line without covering his face or the blade.

Minor only. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch23 row: Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small flush gold ear stud, silver chain, white mundu, and the shoulder cloth over his left shoulder. His shoulder cloth has a gold border, while 11.1 shows it plain. The boy runs LEFT, fully visible and untouched, clear of the blade. The raider's fist is empty and reaches toward Nagoji's sword arm instead of being knotted in the boy's shoulder cloth, so this reads as the instant after the boy twists loose. The beat still lands. Nagoji's left hand is hidden behind the raider's forearm, and this reads as a grapple, not a fused limb. The raider's head cloth and waist cloth are dark maroon, which the setting note reserves as red for Ponnan alone. The colour reads as wine, the raider is bearded and bare-chested in a head cloth, and he is cut off at the right border, so he does not read as Ponnan. There is no text, no blood and no gore, and the panel has no lettering.

Nagoji is in the wrong costume, so he does not match the chapter 23 row or panels 11.1 and 11.4. His curly hair hangs loose down his back with no topknot, and he wears a long-sleeved cream tunic and loose trousers (the commander cut without the turban) instead of a bare-armed white mundu and shoulder cloth. The rest works: the boy runs into the thorn, cloth-covered bodies lie on the rocks with no blood, and the talwar hangs at Nagoji's side with his back to us.
decisions.correction: Nagoji, seen from behind in the foreground, must wear the chapter 23 Ananthan Pillai dress exactly as in panel 11.1: his long curly black hair gathered into a Kerala topknot high on the crown, with first grey at the temples (never loose curls down the back, no turban). His back and arms are bare, with the cream shoulder cloth draped over one shoulder and a white ankle-length mundu wrapped at the waist. No long-sleeved tunic, no trousers, no sash. The silver chain of office shows at the side of his neck, and a small gold ear stud is visible. The talwar hangs down at his side in his right hand, its blade dulled dark, never red. Keep the composition: the boy small in the mid-ground, feet slipping on rock as he disappears into the thorn scrub; cloth-covered bodies and dropped spears and matchlocks on the rocks, no blood; drifting smoke and a rock face behind.

decisions.issues: Minor only: a thin dull orange-brown waistband shows under the mundu fold at Nagoji's waist. It is not a broad red sash, but it is worth a glance. His chain of office is a thin beaded chain rather than the heavier chain in 11.1. Padmini's bay has a small white star on its forehead, a detail the bible does not fix. The beat is correct: a sunset ridge, rows of cloth-covered bodies dragged into lines on the valley floor, and Padmini on her horse with grey threading her coiled hair, cream sari with gold border, gold jewellery. Nagoji climbs up on foot (topknot, grey, stud, moustache, clean chin, silver chain), his mundu and forearms soaked to the elbows in dark brown stains, never red. The wide sunset sky across the top takes all four lettering lines.

Minor only: at 6x zoom, the gold border on Ponnan's sleeve breaks into faint capital-letter-like glyphs. At the frame's own size and at print size they read as ornamental pattern, but they could be smoothed in retouch. A small background bullock driver by the gun carriage wears a red head cloth, against the rule that red cloth is Ponnan's alone this chapter. The light gun on its bullock carriage matches the chapter's column (2.1, 4.3). The beat is correct: Ponnan (curly hair, no topknot, heavy moustache, red shoulder cloth over a short red jacket, white mundu) wipes his spear with a cloth, and Padmini turns her horse away, looking back over her shoulder (grey in her coiled hair, cream sari with gold border, walking stick). It is the same sunset ridge as 11.4. The open sky above both heads takes the two speech lines.

Acceptable with minor drift. The hall matches the script: laterite walls, carved teak ceiling, grey stone floor, brass lamps and a tall doorway at the far end. Ramayyan matches his sheet at the low desk, with the palm-leaf strips fanned, the cord loose and the stylus in hand. Nagoji has a topknot, grey temples, gold stud, curled moustache, silver chain, mundu and shoulder cloth, and stands stiffly with his hands clasped. The scar is correctly on his LEFT forearm. Padmini has her chin high and her stick. Minor points: Varma has a grey temple streak and a gold stud earring, so he reads close to Nagoji (he wears pearl drops in 12.2). His hair knot sits at the back of his head, not above the left ear. He stands in thought rather than pacing. Nagoji's chin has faint stubble shading. There is no text. Lettering: the caption goes top-left over the ceiling, Ramayyan's balloon over the wall and window left of Varma, and Nagoji's over the ceiling above the doorway.

Acceptable. This fixes the r1 failure: Varma is now the only figure, with no second Varma or Nagoji double at the desk. He matches his V13 sheet: curled moustache, red-and-white namam on the brow, pearl drop earrings, gold bead necklace, cream-and-gold cloth over the shoulder, bare chest and cream mundu. He has no turban, crest or crown. He turns back over his shoulder with a cold sidelong glare, which carries the 'stops pacing and turns' beat. The hall matches 12.1, 12.3 and 12.5: laterite walls, timber pillars, a carved teak ceiling, a grey stone floor, brass lamps and a tall doorway with daylight. His back is unmarked, which is correct because the wound comes only from 16.1. His visible right fist is sound. There is no text or pseudo-text. Minor drift: his hair is more silver at the temple than in 12.1, where he has only a grey streak, and his knot sits at the back of his head rather than above the left ear. Both match how 12.1 drew him. Lettering: put the short line over the carved ceiling just right of his face (x 0.45 to 0.7, y 0.03 to 0.2). Put the medium line over the ceiling and the plain laterite wall at upper right (x 0.6 to 0.97, y 0.15 to 0.35). Both stay clear of his face and fist.

Clean. Padmini (grey threading in her hair, gold necklace and stud earrings, cream sari with gold border, stick) cuts in with an open hand. Ramayyan matches his sheet, seated at the low desk and snapping back with the stylus pointed. The hands are sound. It is the same hall, with the same lamps and doorway, as 12.1. There is no text. Lettering space: Padmini's balloon over the ceiling and pillars between the two heads; Ramayyan's two balloons over the ceiling and wall above his head at upper right.

Acceptable. This fixes the r1 failure: Nagoji is alone, with no older Nagoji double at the desk. He matches his sheet and the chapter 23 bible row: Kerala topknot high on the crown, first grey at the temples, a small flush gold ear stud, a thick curled moustache and a clean-shaven chin. He wears a silver chain, a white mundu and a cream shoulder cloth with gold and green borders. He has no turban and no sash. The flush rising in his neck is clearly painted in red, and his clenched fists are sound. The brand on his LEFT forearm is now a pale, pinkish ridged patch next to the long white scar line, not a dark glyph. It sits on the upper outer forearm near the elbow rather than the inner forearm above the wrist, which is a minor placement drift. There is faint stubble shading on the chin, also minor. The memory inset in the lower right is correct: a hard border, sepia, the boy's raised open hands against the rock, five fingers each, only the back of his head, and no face or blade. It is the same hall as the other panels on the page. There is no text. Lettering: the upper right laterite wall is large and plain. Put Nagoji's medium line just right of his face (x 0.38 to 0.65, y 0.04 to 0.22). Put Varma's long off-panel line over the wall at right (x 0.66 to 0.97, y 0.08 to 0.45), above the inset, with its tail to the right edge where Nagoji is looking.

Acceptable. Nagoji kneels on the floor with his head bowed, rather than standing and bowing his head. It is a stronger submission than the script asks for, but it carries the beat. His look matches: topknot, grey temples, gold stud, curled moustache, silver chain, scar on the LEFT forearm. The brand is only a small dark smudge, barely visible. Ramayyan is unmoved at the desk and matches his sheet. Padmini's head is turning sharply toward the right. She is in frame, so her '(off)' line's tail point is set at her own mouth. It is the same hall as 12.1 and 12.3. There is no text. Lettering space: Nagoji's balloon goes top-left over the pillars, Padmini's over the ceiling or doorway sky near her head, and Ramayyan's over the wall above him at upper right.

Minor only: Varma has no namam on his brow here (he wears one in 12.2 and 13.2) and his knot sits at the back of the head rather than clearly above the left ear. Nagoji matches the bible: topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold ear stud, silver chain, faint marks on the LEFT forearm. Ramayyan and Padmini (grey threading through her hair) match their sheets. The ceiling band and the space above the doorway are clear for both Padmini balloons.

Minor only. Varma's hair is noticeably grey-streaked and the knot sits at the back of the head toward his left rather than squarely above the left ear, but this matches the Varma already kept in 13.1 (grey-flecked hair, seated on the same red cushioned seat). The round-1 failure is fixed: the extra off-model scribe is gone and Varma is alone, gesturing calmly toward frame left where Padmini stands. No bandage, which is correct because the knife wound only comes at 16.1. He has the V13 face, namam, pearl drops, gold beads, a cream-and-gold cloth and no turban or crest. The laterite hall has timber pillars, brass lamps and the doorway. Both hands are sound, there is no text, and the upper-left laterite wall gives a large clear area for the long balloon.

Clean. Padmini is alone and on-model: thick black hair threaded with grey and coiled at the nape, gold ear studs and bead necklace, a cream sari with a narrow gold border in the old drape with no blouse, and the long walking stick in her right hand, with a sound grip. Her disgusted sideways look goes toward frame right, toward the king, which fits 13.2, where Varma faces left toward her. The setting is the same laterite and teak hall with brass lamps and the far doorway, and there is no text. The plain laterite wall at upper left, between the pillar and her head, holds both balloons with short tails to her mouth.

Framing deviation: the script asks for the three men 'small in the hall'. Here Varma (left, gold beads) and Nagoji (right, seen from behind) are large foreground figures, with Padmini small in the doorway. The beat still reads: Padmini's back going out through the tall doorway, her stick planted on the grey stone, Ramayyan correct at his desk, and the three men left behind watching. Nagoji's brand and scar show on the back of his LEFT forearm in this rear view, with no letters and no cross. This is a silent panel, so no lettering space is needed.

Clean; the round-1 three-hand error is fixed. Ramayyan has exactly two hands: the right writes with the iron stylus on flat, open palm-leaf strips with the cord loosened, and the left lifts in a small dismissive wave while his eyes stay on the leaf. His face matches the sheet: thin, receding hair with curly sides, plain white cloth. Nagoji is on-model: topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, a small flush stud (it reads slightly pale), silver chain, white mundu and cream shoulder cloth, and no turban or sash. He bows with palms joined, stepping toward frame right to go. His left forearm shows only a thin pale line, not a dark glyph. The hall matches the page, and there is no text. The ceiling and laterite wall above and left of Ramayyan's head leave room for his two balloons, clear of both faces and the waving hand.

Minor, acceptable: the shoulder cloth is still draped over his right shoulder rather than set aside (a folded striped cloth on the side table partly covers the beat). The left-forearm brand is drawn near the elbow as a small concentric-ring mark with a pinkish scar line, not a pale puckered patch a hand's width above the wrist (no letters or cross). The chain-of-office medallion has tiny notches around its rim that read as ornament, not legible script. Light stubble shading on the jaw, which reads as shading at print size. Beat, lamp, topknot with grey at the temples, gold ear stud, raw red knuckles and faintly pink water all work. Captions fit the plain dark wall at upper left or upper centre.

Minor, acceptable: the knuckles are no longer visibly raw. The left forearm shows a brown blotch and a pale oval near the wrist, with the white scar running across the arm instead of along it. A faint white line also appears on the right forearm. Padmini has a tiny dark dot between her brows that is not on her sheet. The doorway is on the left here and on the right in 14.1, which can read as the reverse angle of the same room. Beat, shawl, still walking stick, topknot, chain and ear stud are all correct. The plain wall between the figures (and the night sky in the doorway) gives room for all three balloons.

v01: Nagoji wears no silver chain of office, though the chapter 23 bible row requires it and 14.1 and 14.2 show it. The brand on his inner left forearm is a crisp drawn circle with a line through it, like a phi or null sign, so it reads as a pseudo-letter and not as a pale puckered patch. Padmini has lost the shawl she wore pulled tight in 14.2 (and that 14.5 calls for). Composition, lamp between them, faces and the wall space for lettering are good.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition exactly: Padmini stepping in through the doorway at left, leaning forward on her long walking stick, frowning; Nagoji seated cross-legged on the woven mat at right, looking up at her; the clay lamp on its stool and the brass basin on the floor between them; the plain laterite wall above. Fixes: Nagoji wears his silver chain of office around his neck, lying on his bare chest, the same chain as in the previous panel. Padmini wears the same fawn woollen shawl from the previous panel around her shoulders over her cream sari, loosened now as she steps in. The brand on Nagoji's inner LEFT forearm is only a faint, irregular pale patch of puckered raised scar tissue a hand's width above the wrist, blurred and organic, beside the long thin white scar. Do not draw a circle, a line through a circle, any symbol, glyph, letter, numeral, cross or geometric shape there; if in doubt, turn that forearm so the brand is not seen.

decisions.issues: v01: the brand on Nagoji's left forearm is a dark letter-like glyph (like a capital A with a bar over it), which counts as painted pseudo-text and breaks the bible's pale puckered patch. Nagoji wears no silver chain of office (required by the ch23 row and shown in 14.1 and 14.2). Padmini's shawl from 14.2 is missing. The lamp sits on the floor below and between them rather than between their faces. The whisper pose, faces, ear stud, moustache, Padmini's grey threading and the wall space for two balloons all work.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition: Padmini kneeling close at left, leaning in with one hand cupped beside her mouth as she whispers, her long walking stick upright in her other hand; Nagoji seated cross-legged at right in profile, turned to her, listening; the plain laterite wall above their heads and the doorway at right. Fixes: Nagoji wears his silver chain of office around his neck, lying on his bare chest, as in the earlier panels on this page. Padmini wears the same fawn woollen shawl from the earlier panel around her shoulders over her cream sari, loosened. Set the small clay oil lamp on a low wooden stool between them so its flame sits between and just below their two faces, lighting both. The brand on Nagoji's inner LEFT forearm is only a faint, irregular pale patch of puckered raised scar tissue a hand's width above the wrist, blurred and organic, beside the long thin white scar. Do not draw any dark tattoo-like mark, glyph, symbol, letter, numeral, cross or geometric shape on either arm.

decisions.issues: Acceptable with logged deviations. The over-the-shoulder view of open, scrubbed hands works, with sound anatomy (thumbs on the correct sides, five digits each). The brand is on the LEFT wrist as scripted, but it is a crisp dark square stamp with a hollow centre, not a pale puckered patch. It has no letters or cross. White scar lines appear on both wrists, so the right wrist carries a scar the bible reserves for the left arm. The faint pale line across the LEFT palm is not distinct. Ridged nails cannot be seen palms-up; the fingertips show dark purple bruising instead, which reads as old injury, not gore. Padmini is crouched, clutching the end of her cream sari at one bare shoulder rather than straightening with the 14.2 shawl slipping. If 14.3 and 14.4 are regenerated with the shawl, this will read as the shawl gone. Lettering fits the wall above the lamp and basin and the dark mass of Nagoji's hair at upper left (for the caption).

Minor only. Nagoji has a faint small reddish mark on his brow (the bible's constant identity says no forehead marks), so a retouch is advisable. He holds a spear among the escort, which is acceptable. Otherwise he is correct: topknot, grey temples, gold stud, curled moustache, clean chin, silver chain, white mundu and shoulder cloth, and no turban or sash. Varma's hair is loose with a knot at the back of the crown, not a side knot above the left ear. He correctly has no turban or crest, the pearl drops from his sheet, sandal paste, rings, a white angavastram, and no wound before the attack. Brass lamp stands stand in for most of the belikal stones. The large clear sky at upper left, above the royal party, holds both captions.

Acceptable. The beat is clear: a lean, bare-chested devotee in a plain white mundu with close-cropped hair and three ash lines slips low out of the front of the crowd past the white-clad escort, with the gopuram and elephants behind. Minor points: (1) at full zoom there is a faint thin shadow on his upper lip that could be read as a pencil moustache (the script says NO moustache), but it is barely visible at panel size; (2) the rendering is more painterly than the inked style of 15.1 and 15.4; (3) the escort here wears white turbans, white tunics and leather cross-belts, which should be the reference for 15.3. The open sky at the top centre (x about 0.35 to 0.6, y about 0.03 to 0.2) takes the caption without covering anything.

Minor only. The escort spearmen wear dark leather cross-belts with brass buckles and have beards, so they differ slightly from the plain white-clad spearmen in 15.1. The chaver is correct: close-cropped hair, no moustache, three ash lines on the brow, a curved gutting knife, and a clean leap over the spear line. Anatomy is sound, with no blood and no text. Clear sky at upper left holds both captions.

Acceptable. The heir matches his sheet: sharp cheekbones, wide frightened eyes, white namam, thin gold chain, small white mundu. He is frozen on the flagstones with one hand raised as the curved knife comes down at him from the upper right, with the gopuram, elephants and escort behind. Minor points: (1) his hair is a loose curly mass rather than the sheet's neat topknot (the topknot is only required for chapters 17 and 22); (2) his crossed ankles are slightly ambiguous, with one foot hidden; (3) the attacker's mundu has a red border like 15.3, and the background spearmen are bare-chested rather than in the white tunics of 15.2. The inked style matches 15.1. There is caption space in the sky between the gopuram top and the knife (x about 0.36 to 0.54, y about 0.03 to 0.2), or on the flagstones at bottom left.

Minor only. The small background Nagoji has a white namam mark on his brow (bible: no forehead marks) and a gold bangle, so a retouch is advisable. Otherwise he is correct: topknot, grey temples, gold stud, curled moustache, clean chin, silver chain, white mundu, no turban or sash, and his sword half clear of the scabbard. Varma's hair is in a crown knot rather than a side knot above the left ear. Varma correctly shields the heir with his right arm, leaving his back and LEFT shoulder toward the blade, which comes down from the upper right. The attacker appears only as an arm and torso at the right edge. No wound or blood is drawn, the rings and angavastram are correct, and the setting matches 15.1. Clear sky at upper left, beside the gopuram, holds the caption.

Acceptable. The beat is there: Varma spins and drives a ringed fist into the chaver's face, no wound is drawn, and spear points come in from every edge. The chaver has cropped hair, no moustache and horizontal ash lines. The temple court matches 15.5. Minor issues: the chaver wears a rudraksha mala and a white cloth over one shoulder, where 15.3 shows him bare-chested with a thin cord. Varma has grey temples and a red brow dot here, but black hair and a white namam in 16.2. A small spectator's fist near (0.65, 0.70) reads as slightly disembodied against the crowd. There is no lettering, so no space is needed.

Acceptable. Varma's RIGHT hand is correctly clamped to his LEFT shoulder over the white silk, and no blood is shown. The sobbing heir (namam, topknot, thin gold chain, white mundu) clings to his leg. Ramayyan (receding hair, palm-leaf bundle and stylus) pushes through, ashen. The body is not shown. Lettering space: open sky at upper left (x 0.03-0.14) and between the gopuram and Varma's head (x 0.45-0.57, y 0-0.2). Minor issues: the spearmen hold their spears upright instead of lowered in a ring toward the out-of-frame body. Varma's hair is all black here, while 15.5, 16.1 and 17.1 show grey at the temples.

Acceptable. Padmini matches her sheet: grey threading through her black hair (the ch16-27 row), gold stud earring and bead necklace, cream sari with a gold border and no blouse, walking stick. She pulls the heir into her arms. The heir (namam, topknot, gold chain, white mundu, wide watchful eyes) matches. The hands are sound and the temple court matches 16.1 and 16.2. There is plenty of open sky at upper left and upper centre for the single balloon. Minor: her hair is a full curly mass rather than a tight nape coil.

Minor only. Varma's hair knot sits high at the crown and toward the back, not clearly a side knot above his left ear. Nagoji's grey is heavier than 'first grey at the temples'. His gold ear ornament is a small bead close to the lobe rather than a perfectly flush stud. His forearm scar and brand show on the outer face of the crossed left forearm. Everything else is correct. Nagoji has a clean-shaven chin, a thick curled moustache, a topknot, no turban or sash, a silver chain, and he stands by a pillar. Ramayyan is in the doorway with a palm-leaf bundle and stylus, looking uneasy. Varma is bare-chested and bare-headed on a low couch, with physicians binding the back of his LEFT shoulder with green paste and cloth. There is no blood or painted text. The room has a black polished floor, carved timber beams and brass oil lamps. The dark carved ceiling across the top band leaves room for the two captions and both balloons.

Clean. Ramayyan is close and hesitating, with a sideways glance toward screen right, where Varma is off-panel. He matches his sheet: thin sharp features, receding curly hair, plain unbordered white cloth, a palm-leaf bundle and a stylus. His hands are sound. There is no text, the room matches 16.4 (carved timber pillars, black polished floor, brass lamps, a doorway onto the night palms), and there is dark low-detail space in the upper right ceiling and the upper left pillar for the three balloons.

Minor: Varma is already seated upright on the couch, while 17.3 has him 'sitting up', which suggests he was lying back here. Otherwise clean: his eyes are closed, the white bandage is on his LEFT shoulder (screen right), the foreground oil lamp is sputtering with smoke, and the setting is the same lamp-lit black-floored room.

Acceptable with notes. This is a medium shot rather than a close-up, but Varma's open, hard eyes still read. The physician behind him (bare-chested, grey topknot, moustache, forehead mark) looks a lot like Varma and wears no white upper cloth, while the physician in 17.3 does. A cloth draped over the left shoulder hides the bandage, which is plausible because the physician is adjusting it. The ceiling beams at upper left and the pillar area on the left give clear space for both balloons.

Rejected. (1) Anatomy: Varma's pushing forearm has no upper arm of its own. It branches from the same right arm that props him on the cushion, so he has a forked third arm, and his left arm cannot be seen. (2) Blood: there is a red-brown stain on the white dressing at his left shoulder. (3) Consistency: Varma's hair is solid black with a top bun, while 17.1, 17.2, 17.4 and 17.5 give him grey at the temples. Ramayyan is writing on his palm-leaf bundle instead of leaning in. Nagoji (topknot, grey temples, ear stud, silver chain, clean chin, forearm scar) and the room are good.
decisions.correction: Keep the room, the lamp light, the couch, Nagoji (Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, small gold ear stud, silver chain, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, white mundu and cream shoulder cloth) and Ramayyan exactly as they are now, but put Ramayyan's palm-leaf bundle under his arm so he is leaning in toward Varma rather than writing. Varma has exactly two arms with correct anatomy. He sits upright on the low couch with no hand propped on the cushion. His RIGHT arm crosses in front of his chest, with the upper arm clearly attached at his right shoulder, then elbow, forearm and hand all connected, and his right palm pushes the physician's wrist away from his LEFT shoulder. His LEFT arm hangs still at his side. The LEFT shoulder carries a clean white linen bandage with no stain and no red or dark mark of any kind. No limb may emerge from his torso or branch from another arm. Give Varma the same hair as on the rest of this page: bare-headed, a side knot above his left ear, and grey streaks at the temples.

decisions.issues: Clean. This is the true high angle from the carved ceiling, with lamp shadows on the beams in the foreground. Varma lies on the low couch, gazing up, with the white bandage on his LEFT shoulder (screen right). Ramayyan (palm leaves and stylus) is on one side and Nagoji (topknot, grey temples, ear stud, silver chain, clean chin, scar on the left forearm) on the other. The black floor at upper centre, between the couch and the top beam, gives clear space for all three balloons.

Minor issues only. Varma's hair is heavily grey and gathered in a low bun behind his head, not black in a side knot above the LEFT ear as the bible asks. This matches how he is drawn in panels 17.1, 17.2 and 17.4, and the namam, pearl drops and gold beads match 17.1. The whispering hand belongs to his bandaged LEFT arm, which is plausible. Otherwise clean: bare-headed, no crown or turban, bandage on the LEFT shoulder with no blood, the black polished floor, timber pillars, brass open-wick lamps, no painted text. The plain ochre wall at top left (between the pillars) and top right (beside the face and over the doorway) leaves room for three medium balloons without covering the face or hand.

Minor only: Varma's couch shows only as an edge with draped cloth at the left, which reads fine as an off-panel king. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch23 row: topknot with grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold stud, white mundu with cream shoulder cloth, silver chain, and on the LEFT forearm a pale scar and a small brand patch with no letters. The raised hand is sound with five digits. The upper-left wall is clear for the balloon. The black floor, brass lamps and red-and-wood couch match 18.2 and 18.3.

Clean. Chest-up on Varma on the red couch. The white bandage is wrapped on his LEFT shoulder and his RIGHT hand (ring, gold bangle) rests on it. The hand is sound. Varma's sheet face is there: curled moustache, pearl drop earring, gold bead necklaces, Vaishnavite forehead mark, hair knotted back. Hard, flat gaze. Minor: a few grey streaks in his hair. The two long lines fit on the plain dark wall beside and above his head and over the pillars and door at upper right, clear of his face and hand.

Minor only: the brow mark is a red-and-white namam, where 18.2 shows a plain white one. A grey-haired physician at the right edge tends the shoulder, which the setting allows. Varma matches his sheet: bare-headed with no turban or crest, hair knotted, pearl drops, gold bead necklaces, bare-chested in a white gold-bordered mundu. He lies back with his jaw set. The bandage is on his LEFT shoulder (the near side, with his head to frame right) and shows only skin-tone gaps and white paste, no red. The upper-middle wall is wide and clear for the long balloon. The red bolsters and black floor match 18.2.

Acceptable. Nagoji matches his sheet (topknot, grey temples, gold stud, clean-shaven chin, curled moustache, silver chain, white mundu) and looks toward Ramayyan. Ramayyan matches his sheet (receding hair, side curls, ivory cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus) and is grim with his head bowed. Two departures: he is writing on the palm leaf rather than giving a pure nod, which reads as the order being sealed, and the background Varma, small and seen from behind, has short loose curls rather than the side knot. The white cloth over his left shoulder reads as the dressing. No lettering. Hands sound, no text in the art.

Acceptable, with one framing departure. The script asks for the two men to be small in the long perspective. Here they are a large mid-ground pair filling most of the panel height, though the long lamp-lined corridor and the gleaming black floor are prominent on the left. Ramayyan and Nagoji match their sheets and are leaving the open door of the king's room. Both wear leather toe-ring sandals indoors (minor). Lettering: Ramayyan's line fits on the wall left of his head and Nagoji's two lines on the upper wall between the figures and the door and on the plain amber wall at upper right.
